rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst, but it overstates certainty: the embryo appears more like an expanded blastocyst with a visible ICM on the right rather than clearly at 7-8 o'clock, and TE cohesion/absence of degeneration cannot be confirmed so definitively from this single image.
Thoroughly integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, prior live birth, prior failed cycle, sperm parameters, paternal age, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and well structured, with a plausible prognosis estimate tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor issue is some overconfidence in morphology and euploidy assumptions.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice, especially single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst; slight deviation is somewhat overstating the role of paternal age as an indication to discuss PGT-A.

Provides clear next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx assessment, alcohol cessation, and future sperm DNA fragmentation testing; useful though not highly nuanced on transfer protocol details.
